summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted for evaluation of a rash, eye irritation, and sore throat following an allogeneic stem cell transplant for CML in myeloblastic crisis. Initial workup ruled out viral infections, and a skin biopsy confirmed chronic graft-versus-host disease (GVHD) affecting the skin and eyes. Oral lesions suggestive of herpes simplex virus were treated with a 7-day course of valacyclovir. Symptoms improved with increased prednisone, higher-dose tacrolimus, and topical therapies for the skin and eyes. Transaminitis was noted but trended downward, likely related to GVHD or medication effects. Abdominal pain was chronic and unchanged, with a normal CT abdomen. The patient stabilized, symptoms resolved, and she was discharged home with updated immunosuppressive and supportive therapies.
problems: Herpes simplex with other specified complications
